The workflow is organized around three core stages. First, the process begins by importing raw bathymetric data, either directly from the USACE eHydro platform or from user-provided datasets. Once loaded, the data is processed into parallel Bed Elevation Profiles (BEPs) along the dominent flow direction of the channel.

Second, the BEPs are processed using automated bedform detection algorithms that extract various parameters such as bedform height or length.

Third, the processed results are visualized using built-in plotting tools. These plots are used for inspection, interpretation, and quality control.

This tool also supports batch processing of multiple datasets, enabling efficient analysis of large survey collections. All outputs can be exported for use in external tools or further analysis workflows.

While originally developed for the Missouri River, the processing pipeline is fully general and can be applied to any river system worldwide where compatible multibeam raster bathymetry data is
